novelty.justification: The claim proposes a measurement-level adaptation: an SAE-based "feature-level census of multilingual abstraction," predicting "language-agnostic concept features" alongside language-specific ones and a middle-layer peak. Searches for "multilingual sparse autoencoder universal language-specific features," "cross-lingual SAE concept features steering," and "language-independent language-specific neurons middle layers" found close precedents: Lost in Multilinguality (2025) reports language-independent concepts until late language-specific processing, Understanding and Mitigating Cross-lingual Privacy Leakage via Language-specific and Universal Privacy Neurons (2025) identifies universal versus language-specific neurons with middle-layer sharing, and Causal Language Control in Multilingual Transformers via Sparse Feature Steering (2025) already uses multilingual SAE features causally. Moving from those neuron/subspace findings to parallel-context SAE universality scores and concept-level steering is a non-trivial but natural extension rather than a new core mechanistic relationship, so it merits standard novelty.
